essence: A great city of strangers who never greet or touch, where every crossing of glances kindles a whole imagined affair that dissolves within a second, so that desire circulates endlessly through the most chaste of cities.
textDetails: Chloe is a great city in which everyone moving through the streets is a stranger to everyone else.
At each encounter people imagine a thousand things about one another: meetings, conversations, surprises, caresses, bites.
No one greets anyone; looks cross for an instant and flee toward other looks, never settling.
The first passers-by named: a girl twirling a parasol on her shoulder and swaying her rounded hips; a woman in black who shows her full age, with restless eyes behind a veil and trembling lips.
Then a tattooed giant, a young man with white hair, a female dwarf, and twin girls dressed in coral.
The glances act like lines linking one figure to another, tracing arrows, stars and triangles, until every possible combination is exhausted in a moment.

New characters come on stage: a blind man with a cheetah on a leash (on a chain in the Italian), a courtesan with an ostrich-plume fan, an ephebe, a Fat Woman (Italian 'donna-cannone', the fairground fat lady).
Strangers find themselves together when sheltering from rain under an arcade, crowding beneath an awning of the bazaar, or stopping to hear the band in the square.
There, meetings, seductions, couplings and orgies are consummated with no word exchanged, nobody touching, eyes barely lifted.
The city is constantly stirred by a sensual tremor, yet it is called the most chaste of cities.
Were people to act out their passing dreams, each phantom would turn into a real person, and stories of pursuit, pretence, misunderstanding, clash and oppression would begin.
Then the carousel of fantasies (Italian 'giostra', a merry-go-round) would stop.
Not in the text: any architecture beyond streets, an arcade, the bazaar's awning and a square with a band; the bandstand built as a carousel pavilion is this brief's reading.
visualConcept: A rain-washed piazza on a disc of dark wet cobbles that mirrors every lamp, ringed by tall narrow houses whose streets run off into fog: the city is barely architecture, almost only its crowd. At the centre stands a round bandstand shaped like a carousel pavilion (coral and cream striped cone roof, gilt finial, six tiny musicians), with a curved arcade of lamplit arches behind it and the bazaar's great striped awning to one side. Around the bandstand about 160 small strangers circulate in counter-rotating rings like carousel figures, never colliding and never stopping, and among them walk the named passers-by with unmistakable silhouettes: the girl twirling a parasol, the veiled woman in black, the tattooed giant with faintly glowing linework, the white-haired young man, the dwarf, the coral twins in step, the blind man with his spotted cheetah on a leash, the courtesan with an ostrich-plume fan, the ephebe, the Fat Woman. The conceit is the glance: hair-thin luminous threads flash from head to head, hold for a second and snap, and every few seconds three to six of them close into a triangle, an arrow or a star that flares and dissolves, so a restless constellation of desire hovers at eye level above a crowd that never touches. Nothing physical ever connects: the threads cross the empty space between bodies, and the bodies keep walking. A faint, constant tremor runs through the threads, the lamplight and the reflections in the puddles: the sensual vibration of a chaste city.
layout: North = -z. Wet cobbled disc radius 20 at y=0 with puddle patches (roughness 0.15 against 0.6 elsewhere; fake reflections as vertically stretched additive sprites under each lamp). Piazza radius 8 paved in concentric rings. Bandstand at the centre: octagonal platform radius 1.6, height 0.35, 8 columns 1.3 tall, cone roof to y=2.6 in 16 alternating coral and cream gores, gilt finial; 6 musicians with brass glints. Arcade: north side, 11 arches on an arc at radius 10 spanning about 110 degrees, arch height 1.0, depth 1.0, two storeys above (total 2.3), a lamp in each arch. Bazaar awning: south-east, centred near (6, 0, 6), a 6 x 4 scalloped striped canopy on 6 poles at height 1.3 over 5 stalls. Six streets 2 wide radiate from the piazza (avoiding the arcade and awning), lined out to radius 20 by tall narrow houses (0.9 to 1.4 wide, 3 to 5 storeys of 0.4) with warm windows; 16 lamp posts (1.1 tall) on the piazza rim. Crowd: about 160 anonymous figures (0.25 tall; muted greys, slate blues, browns) on three orbits round the bandstand (radius 3.4, 5.2, 7.0; alternating directions; 0.3 to 0.5 units/s) plus traffic along the streets, with separation steering so no two ever touch. Named characters: 12 figures plus the cheetah (giant 0.42 tall, dwarf 0.15, Fat Woman 0.25 tall and twice as wide, twins identical). Glance threads at head height (y about 0.23) between figures less than 6 units apart.
signatureMotion: 1) Glances: 20 to 40 threads exist at any moment; each shoots from one head to another in 0.12 s, glows 0.5 to 1.2 s and snaps; about every 3 s a cascade links 3 to 6 nearby figures into a closed triangle, an arrow or a star that flares in the bloom and dissolves, and when a cluster's combinations are spent a named character enters from a street to restart the play. 2) The carousel: the rings of strangers circulate round the bandstand like a merry-go-round, the band's tempo visible as slow ripples spreading across the puddles; the parasol spins, the fan opens and shuts, the cheetah's tail flicks, the twins keep step. 3) Showers every 40 s or so: drizzle streaks make the crowd condense under the arcade and the awning, where the thread network grows densest, then disperse; throughout, a fine 6 to 8 Hz shimmer trembles in every thread, lamp and reflection.
interactionDescription: Plays the counterfactual the text names: every phantom becomes a person. Threads thicken into solid coral-red cords that bind figures in pairs; pairs stop walking and act out small stories (one chases another round the bandstand, two collide and recoil, one looms over another who kneels, two turn their backs on each other), the carousel rings halt, the band freezes, the shimmer dies and colours drain toward grey. Toggling back dissolves the cords into light and the chaste circulation resumes.
mood: Blue hour right after a summer shower: plum sky with a last rose glow low in the west, warm gas-gold lamps under the arcade and round the square, wet stones doubling every light, soft humid air with a little drifting mist; intimate, charged and elegant, never sordid. Light drizzles come and go.
caption: In Chloe nobody knows anybody, and nobody stops imagining. A glance leaves the girl with the parasol, touches the tattooed giant, slides to the blind man and his cheetah, to the twins in coral, and in that second a whole romance is lived and ended. Under the arcade, beneath the bazaar's awning, around the band in the square, the threads of looking cross and recross. No one speaks; no hand moves. All evening the city hums with desire and stays perfectly chaste.
motto: A thousand love affairs a minute, and not one touch.
camera: Three-quarter view from the south-west, distance about 30 units, elevation about 35 degrees, target the bandstand at (0, 0.8, 0): the arcade arcs across the back of the frame, the bazaar awning sits at frame right, and the piazza ring with its thread network fills the centre; tilt-shift focus band on the piazza so the threads read crisply.
